chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not have the foolish women nurse your children, for the milk transmits [characteristics], and indeed the child is drawn to the milk.' This means the wet-nurse in terms of foolishness and lack of intellect.

key_terms.اَلْحُمْقَاءَ: the foolish women (plural of foolishness/lack of intellect)

ai.seo_question: Why should one avoid having foolish women nurse their children according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) elucidates the Prophet’s advice against employing foolish women as wet-nurses, highlighting the physiological and spiritual mechanism where milk transmits the nurse's innate traits. The phrase 'the child draws to the milk' signifies a natural affinity, suggesting that the wet-nurse's lack of intellect (humn) can be inherited by the child, thereby influencing their character development. This underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the profound impact of wet-nursing (radāʿ) on lineage and temperament, extending beyond mere nutrition to spiritual and intellectual inheritance.
